messages:
ashwin: ran a quick bench comparing streaming vs polling endpoints across regions + GPUs. gist: https://gist.github.com/redwood/bench-livepull

ashwin: testbed: atlas-7b-fp16, quantized int8 fallback, kernels: cuBLAS baseline vs Triton op-fusion, regions: us-west1, eu-west1

claire: nice. what's the payload size and max sequence?

ashwin: payload ~120 tokens avg, max_seq=1024, batcher config: max_tokens=4096, continuous batching ON for streaming

ben: summary numbers:
```
Model,HW,Endpoint,concurrency,p50(ms),p95(ms),p99(ms),tps
atlas-7b-fp16,A10,HTTP-poll,200,48,130,340,820
atlas-7b-fp16,A10,SSE,200,36,150,460,700
atlas-7b-fp16,A10,WS,200,38,115,330,760
atlas-7b-int8,A100,WS,400,30,85,120,1500
```

ben: key takeaway: streaming (SSE) gets lower median but worse p99 under backpressure on A10 because of kernel scheduling; WS slightly more stable.

sophie: did you try disabling continuous batching for streaming in the runtime? can we reduce p99 by limiting per-request batch size?

ashwin: yes, toggled continuous_batch_size cap from 64->16, p99 dropped ~20% but throughput also dropped ~18%

infra-bot: deploy-note: kernel switch to Triton-fused on eu-west1 queued for 2am UTC canary

claire: region diffs: eu-west1 had ~12% higher p99 on A10 vs us-west1, likely due to kernel versions + CUDA driver mismatch

ben: quantization notes: int8 improved throughput significantly on A100 (higher memory BW) but on A10 we saw lower improvement and some decoding stalls

sophie: action items: (1) add kernel-version to per-region metrics (2) add canary config to reduce streaming batch cap (3) update sizing table for Dedicated reservations

ashwin: I'll update the sizing doc and attach new charts. plotting script: `python tools/plot_tradeoffs.py --input=bench.csv --split=endpoint,hw,region`

claire: also add a note about graceful degradation: prefer WS fallback -> HTTP-poll when SSE backpressure detected :warning:

ben: +1, add fallback policy in router config and test with chaos injection

sophie: I'll own the canary and the router policy test. tagging @devops for kickoff :rocket:

devops: got it, will schedule canary and monitor token-level latency dashboards :chart_with_upwards_trend:

ashwin: thanks all — next status update in #eng-ml after canary. smaller follow-ups in PRs.
